chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about an elderly man who is weak and unable to fast during the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'He should give charity in the form of feeding one poor person for each day as a substitute.'

key_terms.صَوْمِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the substitute for fasting for an elderly person who cannot fast?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for the elderly or chronically ill who cannot fast and have no hope of recovery, the obligation is exclusively *fidyah* (feeding a poor person per day) rather than *qada* (making up the fast later). This ruling highlights the jurisprudential distinction between temporary inability, which requires makeup, and permanent incapacity, which requires compensation through charity, reflecting the divine ease (*taysir*) in Islamic law.
